answer:
An exact determinantal formula valid for every allowed nonzero b is
\[\boxed{\Delta_b=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}\mathcal B_S-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}\mathcal B_O-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}\mathcal B_L.}\]
The finite matrices are defined as follows. Put
\[h=2g-2,\quad q=2g-1,\quad N=4g-4,\quad d=q-k=g+r-1,\quad J=\lfloor N/k\rfloor,\quad M=N+Jd+1,\quad P=Jd+h+1.\]
Set \(s=(1-t^{4g+2})^{1/2}\), \(a=-\tfrac12t^{-h}s\), \(\phi=\phi_b\), and \(\psi=t^k\phi\). Define
\[A_{\ell n}=\binom{-n/k}{\ell}(-k\psi)^\ell,\qquad B_{\ell n}=\binom{1-n/k}{\ell}(-k\psi)^\ell,\qquad A_{-1,n}=0.\]
Define Laurent-series matrices \(T_O,T_S,T_L\), indexed by fiber degrees \(0,\ldots,N\), with two components for \(T_S\). Entries vanish unless \(m=n+\ell k\) for an integer \(\ell\geq0\); for such indices set
\[(T_O)_{mn}=t^nA_{\ell n},\qquad (T_L)_{mn}=at^nB_{\ell n},\]
\[(T_S)_{mn}=\begin{pmatrix}at^nA_{\ell n}&0\\-at^{n-1}A_{\ell n}-at^{n+k}\phi' A_{\ell-1,n}&t^nB_{\ell n}\end{pmatrix}.\]
Let
\[\Lambda_M=\{\lambda\in\mathbb Z:0\leq\lambda\leq M,\ \lambda\text{ even or }\lambda\geq2g+1\},\qquad f_\lambda=t^{-\lambda}s^{\lambda\bmod2}.\]
For each such transition matrix T define the finite matrix
\[\mathcal B(T)_{(i,e),(j,\lambda)}=[t^e]\bigl(T_{ij}(t)f_\lambda(t)\bigr),\qquad -P-M\leq e\leq-1,\quad\lambda\in\Lambda_M,\]
where i and j run over all component indices of T. Finally, \(\mathcal B_O=\mathcal B(T_O)\), \(\mathcal B_S=\mathcal B(T_S)\), and \(\mathcal B_L=\mathcal B(T_L)\). All series are expanded at t=0. The ranks are the actual ranks at the specified entire coefficient vector b, not generic ranks.
